papers.title: JEPA-Anything: Learning Predictive Models across Different Worlds
papers.authors: Taoyong Cui, Zhongyao Wang, Xinyue Xu, Weiyang Liu, Zhaochen Yu, Yuying Zhang, Qiang Gao, Mengyue Yang, Wanli Ouyang, Pheng Ann Heng, Yingcheng Wu, Zhenfei Yin, Ling Yang
papers.summary: Extends JEPA with orthogonal predictive factorization, using one predictive principle across vision, biology, clinical trajectories, control, molecular dynamics, physical fields, and weather. It reports gains on all ten matched dynamics tasks, long-horizon molecular rollouts, and experimental support for a nominated biological intervention.
papers.use: This is the closest match to the idea of defining a closed biological system as a world and revisiting network biology as a world model. PerturbRx-style treatment-conditioned transitions may be reframed as factorized predictive dynamics rather than a domain-specific architecture.
papers.steal: Factorize latent targets into complementary predictive components, train dedicated pathways, and recombine them. For OncoGraph, the factors could correspond to structure, biological state, intervention, and observation process.
papers.doubt: The cross-domain claim is unusually broad. Check whether domain-specific encoders, losses, or tuning account for the gains, and whether the biological factor nomination was prospective rather than selected after seeing results.

papers.title: When AI Generates Covariates: Causal Typing and Estimand Drift in Sequential Experiments
papers.summary: Shows that AI-generated features can silently change the causal question when their roles are left unspecified. It proposes a versioned representation map, causal-role classifier, claim-status filter, and estimand lock for sequential experiments.
papers.use: This is directly relevant when PerturbRx latent transitions or LLM-derived OncoGraph edges become downstream covariates. A useful representation can introduce post-treatment leakage or estimand drift unless its causal role is explicit.
papers.steal: Before using any generated feature, record its version, causal role, and claim status, then lock the estimand before analysis.
papers.doubt: The theory assumes correct auditing, but classifying the causal role of an LLM- or graph-derived feature can itself be wrong. Robustness to role misclassification needs empirical sensitivity analysis.

papers.title: BioPhys-Bridge: A Benchmark for Interdisciplinary Scientific Reasoning in Physics-Grounded Biological Research
papers.summary: Builds 500 biophysics cases and 1,517 tasks linking evidence IDs, values, units, equations, assumptions, mechanisms, and next experimental decisions. Even the best reported model reaches only 0.360 evidence-ID F1.
papers.use: Its schema is a strong template for turning OncoGraph from entity retrieval into a research system that connects literature evidence, quantitative models, biological mechanisms, and experimental decisions.
papers.steal: Attach values, units, assumptions, mechanisms, and next decisions to evidence edges, then evaluate evidence-ID F1 rather than only entity or relation accuracy.
papers.doubt: Only 81 of 500 cases received domain-expert review, and the benchmark is single-authored. Annotation reliability, source coverage, and contamination need independent auditing.

papers.title: Dynamic Generalized Gromov-Wasserstein Optimal Transport
papers.authors: Junda Ying, Zhiwei Zeng, Peijie Zhou, Lei Zhang
papers.summary: Generalizes structure-aware Gromov–Wasserstein transport to continuous dynamics with a simulation-free formulation and travelling-pair flow matching. It improves spatial-structure preservation and continuous 3D reconstruction in spatial transcriptomics.
papers.use: This offers a route from Euclidean latent shifts toward dynamics that preserve both expression and tissue or network topology across samples and time points.
papers.steal: Combine feature matching and relational-structure matching in a path action, then marginalize pairwise interactions into one vector field.
papers.doubt: Better spatial reconstruction does not necessarily imply correct cell trajectories. It should be falsified against known lineage or intervention correspondences.

papers.title: PosteriorBench: From Point Estimates to Posterior Matching in Evaluating Generative Inverse Solvers
papers.authors: Jiachen Yao, Zi-Siang Hsu, Xi Deng, Aditi Gupta, Xin Ju, Sally M. Benson, Gege Wen, Anima Anandkumar
papers.summary: Evaluates generative inverse solvers against high-fidelity reference posteriors rather than only a best reconstruction. Five metrics separate point accuracy, uncertainty, distributional alignment, and frequency fidelity.
papers.use: Perturbation and drug-response problems can have multiple compatible trajectories. This suggests evaluating whether models preserve uncertainty and modes rather than reporting only point AUROC.
papers.steal: Measure posterior mean and standard deviation errors, MMD, sliced Wasserstein distance, and power-spectrum error together.
papers.doubt: The benchmark depends on reference posteriors available in four physics tasks. Biology rarely provides such ground truth, so translation beyond simulation is the main challenge.

papers.title: Large Language Model Agents for Evidence Based Genetic Disease Severity Classification
papers.authors: Tohid Ghasemnejad, Ahmadreza Argha, Mark Grosser, John Wang, Min Yang, Thantrira Porntaveetus, Tony Roscioli, Nigel H. Lovell, Mahmoud Aarabi, Hamid Alinejad-Rokny
papers.summary: Uses a ReAct-plus-RAG agent with ACMG/ACOG criteria and PubMed evidence to classify 10,211 HPO terms, independently verify claims, and aggregate severity across gene-disease pairs.
papers.use: This is a concrete example of combining rules, ontology, and PubMed evidence into provenance-bearing decisions, with direct relevance to disease and phenotype layers in OncoGraph.
papers.steal: Separate retrieval, decision, and independent claim verification, and report evidence support at the claim level rather than only final-label accuracy.
papers.doubt: The very high accuracy requires careful checks for overlapping panels, retrieval leakage, ambiguous expert labels, and whether evaluation is genuinely patient-disjoint.

papers.title: MaSCoD: A Multi-Agent Framework for Structural-Context-Guided Candidate Causal Graph Generation
papers.authors: Yudai Nakada, Yuichiro Nishiura, Jin Michael Splichal
papers.summary: Organizes candidate third variables and local structural hypotheses before direct causal-edge judgment. This improves recall but also raises false positives, with strongly dataset- and backbone-dependent results.
papers.use: For OncoGraph, it argues against one-shot LLM edge generation. Enumerating mechanisms, confounders, and mediators first, then filtering with evidence, is a stronger design.
papers.steal: Optimize early candidate generation for recall and audit exactly which reference edges are lost at each reconciliation stage.
papers.doubt: Small benchmarks such as Sachs may overlap with model knowledge. The retention-selectivity trade-off needs testing on temporally held-out, unfamiliar domains.

papers.title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
papers.authors: Run-Ze Fan, Zihao Zhang, Simin Ma, Yebowen Hu, Shouju Wang, Kaiqiang Song, Fei Liu, Hamed Zamani, Xiaoyang Wang
papers.summary: Decomposes coding-agent harnesses into planning, action space, and context management across four models and 176 matched settings. Rule-based elision before LLM summarization is efficient, while planning mainly reduces cost for stronger models.
papers.use: This gives empirical guidance for improving the current Codex and Claude research workflow at the harness-component level rather than attributing everything to model quality.
papers.steal: Fix the execution loop and run matched ablations of context strategy, context budget, planning, and tool surface, including trajectory stopping behavior.
papers.doubt: Coding-benchmark conclusions may not transfer to scientific agents that must preserve evidence and experimental validity.

papers.title: SoL-Pi: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness
papers.authors: Haozhe Liu, Tian Ye, Sensen Gao, Qihang Cao, Yitong Li, Mingchen Zhuge, Duomin Wang, Ruihua Zhang, Ping Luo, Jiawang Bian, Lei Zhu, Ligeng Zhu, Enze Xie, Song Han
papers.summary: Recursively searches agent-harness improvements across diverse environments and retains mechanisms in execution, compaction, observation handling, and delegated reading. It reports similar performance with 44.7–49.0% less token traffic.
papers.use: Across multiple research repositories, reusable harness improvements may accumulate more value than task-specific prompts. This is relevant to making automated research loops cheaper and less lossy.
papers.steal: Retain a harness modification only if it survives selection across multiple heterogeneous environments.
papers.doubt: Transfer from 51 EdgeBench tasks to unseen scientific workflows is unproven, and implementation differences may affect the token-cost comparison.

papers.title: Embedding Models Measure in Peculiar Ways
papers.summary: Tests whether embedding similarity respects objective measurements such as mass, distance, time, and volume. The geometry is weakly aligned with physical measurement and strongly influenced by superficial string similarity.
papers.use: Dose, time, and response magnitude may enter embeddings without their quantitative structure being preserved. This is a useful sanity check for PerturbRx latent geometry and knowledge-graph embeddings.
papers.steal: Unit-test embedding geometry using quantities with known equivalence, ordering, and scale transformations.
papers.doubt: The findings concern text embeddings and may reflect number tokenization rather than general biological representation failure.
